ROLE: Honour a valid DISCONNECT by releasing the connection immediately: the descriptor is closed, queued output is discarded without flushing and the session becomes CLOSED while the registry entry waits for broker_reap.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static enum broker_result handle_disconnect(struct broker *b, struct session *s)
SIGNATURE.NAME: handle_disconnect

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: connection whose subscriptions and descriptor are released when it is destroyed

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: discard queued output, close the descriptor, enter CLOSED

FUNC.NAME: session_state
FUNC.ROLE: the resulting SESSION_CLOSED state observed by the caller

VAR.NAME: BROKER_CLOSE
VAR.ROLE: the session is closed and must be reaped by the caller

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the queued-output buffer is released, the descriptor is closed exactly once, the state becomes SESSION_CLOSED; nothing is written to the peer
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases the session's descriptor and queued bytes; the session object and its stored subscriptions are freed later by broker_reap through session_destroy, so other sessions are untouched
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; already CLOSED sessions are left unchanged, which makes the DISCONNECT path safe if a failure already closed the same session

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the session's current state; SESSION_CLOSED means the descriptor is already released and the queued output already dropped, so a second teardown attempt is a no-op
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: read-only projection of the target session; the returned enum owns nothing and the session object stays owned by the broker registry
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: NULL s yields SESSION_CLOSED (documented total function); no side effects and no failure else

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker registry (not dereferenced). s: the READY session whose received bytes were the 2-byte DISCONNECT packet already validated by wire_decode_empty(WIRE_PACKET_DISCONNECT) (type 14, flags 0, Remaining Length 0). No payload is read from the input buffer.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. Call session_close_immediately(s): the queued output is released without being flushed, the descriptor is closed exactly once and the session enters SESSION_CLOSED (the call is a no-op if an earlier failure already closed it). 2. Return BROKER_CLOSE so the framing loop stops processing further bytes of this connection and the execution layer reaps the registry.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: BROKER_CLOSE; the session is SESSION_CLOSED with no queued output and a closed descriptor. Its subscriptions and identifier remain reachable through the session object only until broker_reap calls session_destroy, which releases them, so no other connection inherits them and freshly accepted connections always start with an empty subscription list.
INVARIANTS_USED: DISCONNECT is a clean client-initiated teardown: the server closes the connection and keeps no session state
this broker stores no state across connections, so the client's subscriptions simply cease to exist
closing one session never modifies another session's descriptor, queue or subscriptions
queued output of a disconnecting client is discarded rather than flushed
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is non-NULL and in SESSION_READY; the caller already validated that the frame is a complete, well-formed DISCONNECT.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: session_state(s) == SESSION_CLOSED, session_fd(s) == -1 and the session contributes no queued bytes; the registry still contains the entry until broker_reap removes it.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the session is not touched concurrently.

EXPECT.note: the earlier queued PINGRESP is discarded, not written
the descriptor is closed exactly once even if the session was closed before

runtime: client C CONNECT id 'a' then PUBLISH 't/y' payload 'w'

EXPECT.note: client C reusing identifier 'a' starts with no stored subscriptions and receives its own QoS 0 echo
